en.description:
The Senior Communications Officer coordinates and supports International Crisis Group’s media outreach in Africa, with the aim of increasing coverage of Crisis Group’s analysis and policy recommendations on conflict-related issues. Working with a highly professional team of conflict research analysts, the Communications Officer will be expected to use innovative approaches to promote and disseminate Crisis Group’s work. The successful candidate will be based in either Nairobi, Kenya or Dakar, Senegal.

Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement an Africa Program communications strategy, including targeted campaigns, in close coordination with the program director, Africa and liaising with Crisis Group’s communications team;

  • In collaboration with the communications team in Brussels, lead in designing and implementing communication plans for the launch of Crisis Group reports and other publications, with a strong focus on English and French language audiences in Africa;

  • Build and cultivate a strong network of local and international journalists based in Africa; create and maintain a database of media contacts and manage media inquiries;

  • Write op-eds, press statements and other external media materials;

  • Produce or help with the production of audio-visual content in collaboration with the communications team in Brussels – e.g. videos, podcasts, photographs and photo essays;

  • Collaborate with the communications team in Brussels to create and implement multi-channel social media campaigns; help develop the capacity of program staff to share social media content;

  • Organise local media events, including around launches of Crisis Group publications, plan and coordinate press briefings and online/in-person webinars.

Requirements include:

  • A degree in conflict studies, political science, international relations or similar; 

  • At least five years of professional experience in U.S. advocacy or policy environment; appointment at Senior Analyst level requires demonstrated ability to lead advocacy initiatives independently, manage senior stakeholder relationships and exercise sound political judgement on sensitive policy issues; 

  • Proven familiarity with international think tanks, NGOs, and multilateral organisations;  

  • Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of U.S. foreign policy and related institutions;

  • Excellent administrative and organisational skills and an ability to pay close attention to detail; 

  • Excellent oral and written communication skills; and,

  • Authorisation to work in the U.S.

Salary range:
Analyst: USD 68,000 - USD 80,000/year

Senior Analyst: USD 88,000 - USD 100,000/year

Crisis Group offers a comprehensive medical insurance (including vision and dental care) with a 90% employer contribution and a 403(b) pension plan with an employer contribution of 5%. Other benefits include FSA, 25 days leave per year, access to employee assistance program, a.o.

en.description:
The Analyst/Senior Analyst advances Crisis Group’s conflict prevention objectives by informing and influencing U.S. foreign policy through engagement with government officials and other key stakeholders. Reporting to the Program Director, U.S. and working closely with colleagues across programs, the role develops and implements advocacy strategies, builds relationships with policymakers and other stakeholders, and produces research and analysis to support Crisis Group’s engagement in DC. 

 

Responsibilities:

  • Works with colleagues to develop and implement advocacy strategies focused on selected U.S. and U.S.-based stakeholders, including in the Executive Branch, Congress, international organisations, non-governmental organisations, the media, think tanks, academia, and other communities with an interest in conflict prevention and mitigation;

  • Coordinates DC contacts with program and project directors and other Crisis Group staff as needed, to ensure maximum internal awareness of debates and activities, and its adequate reflection in Crisis Group publications;

  • Builds and maintains a bipartisan, cross-agency network of senior officials across Congress and the executive branch, expanding engagement to ensure continuity of access regardless of political transitions;

  • Serves as a key point of contact in monitoring developments in the U.S. government, tracking policy developments and researching issues of cross-cutting organisational relevance, including mediation, conflict prevention, peacekeeping, sanctions etc.;

  • Contributes to reports and other written pieces on U.S. foreign policy, and writes occasional pieces for publication;

  • Deliver oral and written presentations to relevant stakeholders on Crisis Group policy positions and activities in crisis management and conflict mitigation;

  • Represents Crisis Group at meetings with academic institutions, think-tanks, and NGOs, and coordinates with media;

  • In coordination with the President’s office, plans and executes President & CEO advocacy visits to Washington, including stakeholder mapping, meeting strategy, briefing preparation, and follow-up;

  • In coordination with the senior adviser to the President, staffs the President & CEO at major international forums, providing speaker preparation and bilateral engagement strategies aligned with advocacy objectives;

  • Designs, convenes, and executes off-the-record roundtables and stakeholder discussions, independently selecting topics, participants, and formats to stress-test policy options and advance solutions-oriented debate.

offers.requirements:
Responsibilities include:

  • Monitoring political and security-related developments across West Africa and the Sahel via online sources.

  • Writing daily press roundups on countries covered by the projects.

  • Assisting in drafting monthly situation reports on countries covered by the projects.

  • Assisting in various research assignments, including conflict data analysis.

  • Attending in person and virtual events of interest held by International Crisis Group and taking a written note thereof.

  • Attending Crisis Group in person and virtual research meetings where possible and taking a written note thereof.

  • Other administrative tasks as may be required.

Qualifications include:

  • Good writing, research and organisational skills.

  • Good knowledge of international politics related to conflict prevention and demonstrable knowledge of African politics, preferably West Africa/Sahel.

  • Previous experience working in/on West Africa or the Sahel an asset.

  • Ability to summarise information in a concise and clear manner.

  • Good level in both verbal and written English and French required.

  • Knowledge of Arabic, Hausa, Bambara, Tamacheq, Fulfulde, Mooré, or Portuguese strongly preferred.

  • Knowledge of visualisation tools (QGIS, Adobe Illustrator, InDesign, Tableau) an asset.

  • Authorization to undertake an internship in Senegal.

If interested, please apply by 16 November 2026. Interviews will be conducted on a rolling basis, and the application may close earlier if a suitable candidate is identified.

en.description:
Role:

International Crisis Group’s West Africa and Sahel projects are looking for an intern to start in January 2027 to support their project directors and analysts in their daily activities. Requiring a natural flair for politics and foreign affairs, it is an excellent opportunity for someone to learn about conflict analysis and advocacy work but also to gain valuable experience in a high-profile international NGO.

This internship would suit a candidate with an excellent level in both French and English and a recent undergraduate or graduate degree in international relations, political science or related fields. The ideal candidate is someone seeking to gain experience in a fast-paced, international NGO working to prevent and resolve deadly conflict in the region. Based in Dakar, Senegal, the role will involve supporting both the Sahel and West Africa projects by following developments in countries within the region including but not limited to Mali, Burkina Faso, Niger, and the coastal Gulf of Guinea countries.

Internships are available exclusively to students participating in academic or sponsored programs, e.g. students who can integrate the internship into their academic curriculum for credit or those who have secured external funding, such as a grant or scholarship, to support them during the internship.
